To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed, synthesized, and characterized a novel series of organometalic tricarbonyltricarbonyl Re/Tc(I) chelates that are conjugated to a small molecule GPER agonist.

we have designed, synthesized, characterized, and evaluated a series of organorhenium and organotechetium tricarbonyls as potential radiopharmaceuticals for the imaging of GPER expression in human cancers.
the synthesis and characterization of tricarbonylrhenium chelates conjugated to a tetrahydro-1,2,4-triazole GPER ligand was performed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel tricarbonylrhenium(I) chelate probes targeting the G protein-couple estrogen receptor GPER.
the development of new chemical probes and radiotracers for the GPER/GPR-30 receptor.
the development of organometal-based chelate ligands as probes of the GPER/GPR-30 receptor and as radiolabeling precursors for diagnostic imaging agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GPER-selective tricarbonylrhenium and tricarbonyltungsten chelates described here are promising candidates for further development as GPER imaging agents.
this study has provided a new approach to GPER targeting, and that the organometallic chelates developed in this study represent promising leads for further development.
the G protein-couple receptor GPER is a novel and important target for noninvasive imaging and therapy of cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and characterized a new class of organometal complexes for GPER imaging and therapy.
the design and development of GPER-selective organometallic radiotracers has been successful and the results are promising for the future development of GPER-targeted imaging probes.
the design of organometal tricarbonyls conjugated to small molecules can lead to compounds with excellent receptor selectivity and stability in biologically important media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the organometallic chemistry approach to GPER imaging is a promising strategy that is worth pursuing further.
the GPER-selective ligands we have developed have been successfully conjugated to a rhenium tricarbonyldicarbonyl chelating system.

the organometallic chelate structure is a critical determinant in GPER selectivity and activity, and that these properties can be modulated by the choice of chelating moiety and linkage to the GPER-selective pharmacophore.
